'''Boris Frlec''' (10 February 1936 – 18 February 2026) was a Slovenian politician.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Barany |first=Zoltan |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/The_Future_of_NATO_Expansion/txlteD2HG9EC?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=Boris+Frlec&pg=PA102&printsec=frontcover |title=The Future of NATO Expansion: Four Case Studies |date=21 July 2003 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-1-139-44044-8 |language=en}}</ref>
[[File:Boris Frlec 2014.jpg|thumb|Frlec in 2014]]

== Life and career ==
Frlec was born in [[Ljubljana]] on 10 February 1936. He served as the [[Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs (Slovenia)|minister of foreign affairs]] (1997–2000).<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/NATO_Review/0M5ZIPcuQ1AC?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=Boris+Frlec+minister+of+foreign+affairs&pg=RA3-PA16&printsec=frontcover |title=NATO Review |date=1999 |publisher=NATO Information Service. |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Ministry for foreign Affairs |url=https://www2.arnes.si/~quark/MinistryFA/Frlec2.html |access-date=21 February 2026 |website=www2.arnes.si}}</ref>

Frlec died on 18 February 2026, at the age of 90.<ref>{{Cite web |title=STA: Former foreign minister Boris Frlec dies |url=https://english.sta.si/3524156/former-foreign-minister-boris-frlec-dies |access-date=21 February 2026 |website=english.sta.si}}</ref>
